out.reasoning: Starting from the market’s 0.91 estimate, I make a small upward adjustment. Sutcliffe’s October poll lead of 53% to 31% among decided voters is substantial with only 13 days remaining, and September polling independently showed a clear lead. Residents also favor the city’s direction more often than they oppose it, limiting evidence of an anti-incumbent wave. However, 23% remain undecided, the latest survey covers adults rather than explicitly likely voters, and turnout differences or correlated polling error could narrow the lead. His broad geographic support, incumbency, and fragmented opposition strengthen his position under plurality voting. The city-direction findings offer little indication of a strong anti-incumbent wave. However, 23% remain undecided, thirteen days remain before voting day, and turnout differences or correlated polling error could narrow the lead. out.reasoning: Incumbent mayors generally have an electoral advantage, especially against divided opposition. As of October 13, Sutcliffe leads the latest poll by 22 points among decided voters, with geographically broad support; September polling also showed a substantial lead. With only 13 days until election day and advance voting imminent, Leiper needs a major late shift or a large polling/turnout error. The 23% undecided share creates uncertainty, but even substantial opposition consolidation would not automatically erase Sutcliffe’s advantage. Transit dissatisfaction, a serious scandal, or strongly differential turnout could flip the race. Reliance on one recent survey and limited turnout evidence keep the probability below near-certainty.
